piece_title: Enemy AI and behaviour — round 1 critique

build.note: Judged at e97347f with the working tree as found. 41 game/ files carried other agents' uncommitted work throughout; NONE of them under game/src/combat/ or game/data/combat/, both of which were clean and unstaged before and after every ablation (`git status --porcelain -- game/src/combat/ game/data/combat/` and `git diff --cached --name-only` both empty — RULES 17). Every ablation ran on `cp -r game tools` into the scratchpad, never on the tree. NO BROWSER WAS LAUNCHED: `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` returned GO once at the start and exit 3 (4 browser instances, load 21.55 over 4 cores) on every poll thereafter, so I did the work that needs no browser (RULES 21) and marked the two browser-only checks as not independently re-measured. NO TIMING FIGURE APPEARS IN THIS VERDICT — every number is fixed-step geometry, a state count or a trace hash, which contention cannot move.

bifurcation.note: Declared before any artifact was opened. This piece is a state machine and a parameter table; there is no art-direction or fidelity claim in it. The one image in this verdict is a plotted time series produced by my own instrument in bare Node, not a rendered frame, and no visual reference of either era is cited anywhere.

reference_items.native_scale: weighted sum over M1-M9, each 0/1/2, max 18; item's own ladder anchors 12/18=4, 14/18=6, 17/18=8
reference_items.native_verdict: M1 1 (browser, accepted from the builder, not re-measured), M2 2 (same), M3 1, M4 2, M5 2, M6 1, M7 2, M8 2, M9 1. The builder scored 17/18. Three checks move: M3 because RI-AI01 §D T15's RECOVER state is not implemented and M3's `state != COMMIT` therefore excludes every attack-recovery frame (0.0414 -> 0.2521 on the builder's own fixture and seed, all seven fighting statblocks flip 2/2 -> 1/2); M6 because T25's second de-aggro clause is dead code and L_hard is unreachable above the trash tier; M9 because LONG_RECOVERY — one of the three triggers ai.json declares — scores 7/12 against the item's own 80% trial bar. No hard fail on either reading: min_dist_dwell 0.252 < 0.35, CoV 0.1724 >= 0.12, M7 clean at 0.00 deg/s on active/recovery, leash return never invulnerable, no required trace field absent.
reference_items.justification: 14/18 sits exactly on the item's own 6 anchor. Measured mine over the shipping combat modules in bare Node through tools/lib/combat-node.mjs, with my own instrument rather than the builder's; M1 and M2 need the stealth perception model that the arena does not run and are taken from the builder's browser leg.

reference_items.native_scale: weighted sum over the item's checks, each 0/1/2, max 44
reference_items.native_verdict: Only the archetype-distinctness leg was measured, and it is the one this piece's own output decides. The item fails a roster 'if any pair < 1.0 — two archetypes that are the same question in two costumes'. Four of the seven fighting statblocks (inf_trash 412 hp, guard_legion 520, drowned_lesser 260, drowned_greater 640) produce a BIT-IDENTICAL 1,800-frame trace of AI state, position to 0.1 mm, yaw to 0.001 deg and move selection: sha1 1edb362ea24dde99 for all four. Pairwise behavioural distance 0. The roster carries 3 of the item's 10 archetypes against a bar of >= 8. The roster gap itself is inherited and loudly declared by the builder; the absence of any archetype-conditional BEHAVIOUR is this piece's own (prefers_band and blocks are authored with zero readers, DISENGAGE and BLOCK_HOLD are never entered).

checks: game/src/combat/ contains ZERO occurrences of Math.random, of a disposition, faction, bounty, level, wall clock or weather term. Grepped the whole directory; the only hits for 'disposition'/'faction' are English words inside comments.
No to-hit roll and no dice damage anywhere on the enemy path. Hit resolution is geometric (W1-09's, unchanged by this piece).

The AI's six PRNG draws (ai.js:235, 342, 390, 391, 392, 411, 435) all go through the simulation's single counted global core/rng.js instance, exactly as RI-AI01 T11 requires ('seeded PRNG'), and are: T05 roar length, token cooldown, T11 strafe reseed timer, strafe direction, radial sign, and move selection. Move selection draws from a RANGE-GATED eligible pool (_tryCommit filters on dist <= omega + root_dz_m and on stamina before drawing), which is Souls move selection, not a chance mechanic.
NO LEVEL SCALING: no playerLevel / level_scale / levelled-list term reaches world/population.js, character/encounter.js or game/src/combat/.

NO CLOCK INSIDE THE FIGHT: the perception meter reads light and therefore the world clock, but stealth/system.js:405 implements RI-AI01 §B's AGGRO hysteresis ('once AGGRO, drop to SEARCH only via the de-aggro rule, never via meter decay'), so no time of day can drop an aggroed enemy mid-fight. RI-STL01 §1 explicitly owns the multipliers on RI-AI01 §B's fill rates — sanctioned seam, not a leak.

NAMED AND RULED NOT A LEAK, with its call path: sim/step.js -> character/encounter.js::stepEncounters -> openingFor (encounter.js:69) -> behaviour_rule 'hostile_below_disposition' (encounter.js:93) -> character/reaction.js::derivedDisposition({race, upbringing, birthsign}) -> hostile = value < 15 -> aggro_at_m = hostile ? enc.aggro_at_m : null -> stepEncounters writes ctl.alertState='AGGRO' (encounter.js:219) -> combat/ai.js::step reads it (ai.js:186). Live on one shipped encounter, deep-kin-war-brood, hostile below disposition 15, aggro at 18 m. Ruled NOT a leak because (a) the disposition term is BINARY — it decides whether the party is hostile and never modulates aggro_at_m or any frame, band, poise, speed or damage value; (b) ARBITRATION §1 puts the start of the fight at the aggro frame and protects Morrowind's right to parley during one; (c) AR-3 names 'a disposition that opens a door you would otherwise have to fight through' as the crossing the corpus WANTS, and engine.js::spawnEncounter already records the project's standing reading in a comment; (d) S26 warns that a check firing on everything distinguishes nothing. It is one line from being a leak, and that line is `aggro_at_m: 18 - disposition/5`.
ar1.note: Pass. Recorded on my own greps and source reads over game/src/combat/ and game/src/character/encounter.js plus my own PRNG-draw census, not on the builder's assertion.

checks: This piece adds no world-facing surface: no marker, no warp, no procedural loot, no soul purchase, no item-description lore vector. It writes one data file, one decision module and three wiring edits, all inside the fight.
ar2.note: Not applicable rather than pass — there is no Morrowind-side surface for a Souls convention to contaminate here.
ar2.not_applicable_reason: W1-12 adds no Morrowind-side surface for a Souls convention to contaminate. Its whole delta is one new data file (game/data/combat/ai.json), one decision module (game/src/combat/ai.js) and three wiring edits inside the fight, plus a narrowing of one aggro latch. I checked the four shapes AR-2 names and none is present or reachable from anything this piece wrote: no objective marker, no bonfire warp, no procedural loot, no soul-currency purchase, and no item description standing in for NPC dialogue. The one thing that could have leaked outward is the sight-cone gate in character/encounter.js, and it narrows a Morrowind rule with Souls geometry rather than replacing it — W1-07's race_behaviour and hostile_below_disposition rules are untouched, which I confirmed by source read and by the encounter census (1 race_behaviour, 1 hostile_below_disposition, 14 always_hostile; only the always_hostile arm is gated). Recorded as not_applicable rather than pass so that a round-2 critic re-audits it if the piece grows a world-facing surface.

checks: NOT sterile. The piece narrows a Morrowind-side aggro latch (character/encounter.js::stepEncounters, whose rule set includes race_behaviour and hostile_below_disposition) with Souls-side perception geometry — the statblock's own sight cone and a real LOS term — and then hands the resulting alert state to a Souls state machine. The crossing runs in both directions through one file.

It also closes a neighbour's named debt across the seam: game/data/combat/enemies/guard_legion.json said an AGGRO'd guard deals 0 damage and named it W1-12's to close; ai.json's override closes it without editing the statblock.

score.band_label: A real machine that does real work, failing three measurements it makes about itself and one it does not make: RECOVER is absent and that is what carries M3's pass, the enemy cannot close on a walking player, and 30 of 104 shipped behaviour parameters have a reader

status_reasons: 3/10 min-over-axes against a 7.0 wave-1 gate; the reference-item weighted mean is 5.0 and is published alongside so the aggregation is not a hidden choice.
No AR-1 or AR-2 failure, and no RI-AI01 hard fail on either scoring. This is 'below bar with a named remedy', not a void.

The two lowest axes are behaviour-observable (3) and variety (3). The single biggest gap is that the wilderness enemy still cannot reach a player who walks away — the defect the piece was commissioned to fix.

CONSUMPTION at 4 is the axis with the most work in it: 29 of 104 behaviour leaves moved no enemy across four fixtures, and after discounting six for my own instrument's limits, 23 have no reader I can find in game/src by perturbation or by grep.

biggest_gap.what: RUSH is gated on a distance band (dist > 5.0*omega) rather than on whether the distance is actually closing, and APPROACH advances at archetype.*.walk_mps, which for INFANTRY is 2.20 m/s against a player walk of 2.00 m/s. An enemy 10 m from a player walking away in a straight line closes at 0.20 m/s, NEVER enters RUSH in 1,800 frames, never gets nearer than 8.14 m, reaches its 32 m hard leash, oscillates REPOSITION<->LEASH_RETURN for 235 frames at the boundary and walks home. Five of the seven fighting statblocks never enter RUSH against a walking player. The enemy does WORSE against a walking player than a jogging one, because walking keeps the gap just under the band boundary that would trigger a sprint.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the piece's own central question. reports/w1-12/survey.md §3a diagnoses the dead road as (a) 2.20 m/s pursuit against a 2.0 m/s walk, (b) ground handed back during every swing, (c) anchor-based despawn — and §7 claims (a) half-fixed: 'souls archetypes now RUSH at their own declared sprint (INFANTRY 4.6 m/s), which beats a jogging player'. Measured, that is false: the new AI reproduces the pre-piece closure of 0.20 m/s to two decimal places, because archetype.INFANTRY.walk_mps is the same 2.20 as ENGAGE.advance_mps. From the player's chair the wilderness posts still cannot reach them, which is the whole reason this piece exists.

remedy.action: In game/src/combat/ai.js case 'APPROACH', add a closure test alongside the band test: track dist over a rolling window and enter RUSH regardless of band when closure stays below a declared threshold for a declared number of frames; leave RUSH when closure recovers or the band drops to DANCE. Put both numbers in game/data/combat/ai.json under `movement` as rush_when_closure_below_mps and rush_closure_window_f, and give the file a document-level "unit": "f@60" so the frame figure carries its unit (S22).
remedy.acceptance: node tools/combat/critic-w1-12-census.mjs --mode=flee shows entered_RUSH true and min_gap_m <= 0.85*omega for EVERY statblock in the fighting roster at player speeds 2.0 and 3.2 m/s, while the 5.0 m/s row still shows the enemy losing ground (an enemy you cannot outrun at a sprint is a different game). Both new leaves appear in --mode=census's consumed list, not its inert list.

secondary_observations.what: combat/ai.js never enters RECOVER. RI-AI01 §D T15 says an attack leaving `active` becomes RECOVER and T16 returns it to CIRCLE; this build labels the whole swing COMMIT, and M3 counts frames 'while state != COMMIT', so every attack-recovery frame drops out of the denominator. Those are the frames that matter: every attack in the roster carries 0.6-1.2 m of forward root motion, so the enemy ENDS its swing on top of the player and stands there for 20-76 f@60. Measured on the builder's own fixture and seed, all seven fighting statblocks flip M3 from 2/2 to 1/2 — inf_trash 0.0414 -> 0.2521 with 623 of 736 recovery frames inside 0.85*omega; champion 0.0565 -> 0.2425; beast 0.0208 -> 0.1887; caster 0.0443 -> 0.1968. RECOVER is not in the piece's declared_incomplete list the way PATROL, strings and BLOCK_HOLD are. Still short of the 0.35 chase-bot hard fail.

Exhaustive RI-MTH07 census: 104 behaviour leaves in ai.json, 30 with a demonstrated world-side consumer, 45 declared-unrealised archetype rows (honest, excluded), 29 with no consumer across four fixtures. Six of the 29 are caveated by my instrument (x2-only perturbation is a no-op on an already-satisfied threshold; my group fixture is five strong so the <=2 and <=4 token rows cannot fire), leaving 23. Hard core: perception.search_to_leash_frames (T06 unimplemented), perception.suspicious_min_dwell_f, movement.max_yaw_rate_windup_dps and max_yaw_rate_active_dps (§F's yaw legality, read by nothing; the shipped windup steer is hard-coded 180/45 deg/s in enemy.js:259-260), leash.no_los_seconds and leash.dist_multiple_of_sight (this.noLosSinceF is initialised to -1 and assigned NOWHERE, so ai.js:193's branch can never be true), leash.hard_m.elite/.ambusher/.boss (unreachable — leash_tier comes from the archetype row and every shipped statblock resolves to trash), punish_read.react_within_f (a scoring threshold in a game data file; its only reader is ai-probe.mjs), commit.swarm_tokens_at_5_plus (guard requires omega <= 1.8, the roster's smallest is 2.0), and archetype.*.cone_deg at every archetype (12 leaves, no reader anywhere in game/src — the game uses the statblock's sight_cone_deg). Plus three dead duplicates: perception.suspicious_at/aggro_at/decay_per_s, whose live copies are in game/data/stealth/detection.json and are read by stealth/system.js.

Four of the seven fighting statblocks produce a BIT-IDENTICAL 1,800-frame trace of AI state, position to 0.1 mm, yaw to 0.001 deg and move selection: sha1 1edb362ea24dde99 for inf_trash (412 hp), guard_legion (520), drowned_lesser (260) and drowned_greater (640). Four distinct behaviour shapes across seven fighting enemies; every one visits the same five states (APPROACH, CIRCLE, FEINT_STEP, COMMIT, REPOSITION). No archetype-conditional behaviour exists: archetype.*.prefers_band (RANGED/CASTER) has zero readers and DISENGAGE (T24) is never entered, so cst_sap_speaker — which declares "boss": true and "unique": true, and whose own note says a caster that only backs away is a bad enemy — runs the trash-infantry machine and never backs away at all. A sibling piece counted 92 distinct scene-graph signatures.

ai.json's declared_incomplete says 'BLOCK_HOLD (T18) is implemented but unreachable: it is TURTLE-only and no shipped statblock declares archetype TURTLE. The code path exists and the probe reports it as unexercised rather than as passing.' The only occurrence of BLOCK_HOLD in combat/ai.js is the string inside the AI_STATES Set — no branch, no guard, no timer, and archetype.TURTLE.blocks has zero readers. A string in a Set is not a code path. 6 of the 17 declared AI states are unreachable (PATROL, RECOVER, BLOCK_HOLD, STAGGER, DISENGAGE, DEAD); three are declared incomplete, one of those falsely, and two are not declared at all.

Reported because it is the piece's strongest result and a critic should publish what it could not break. 47 of 47 swings across seven statblocks ran to their full declared clip length after the player was teleported 40 m away on the frame the swing began — chop 154/154, thrust 122/122, combo_a 72/72, combo_b 102/102, lunge 92/92, whip 84/84, staff_jab 100/100, shoulder_turn 66/66 — with 0.00 deg/s of yaw on every active and recovery frame. How many frames after an attack starts can the enemy change its mind? ZERO, and it is structural: EnemyController.step() reaches _idleBehaviour() only in the else of `if (b.move)`, so SoulsAI.step() is unreachable for the whole clip, and the retire happens at the top of the step so the AI cannot shorten its own recovery. That matches the reference — Souls enemy attacks are uncancellable and the recovery IS the punish window. I also tried to leak the attack token by staggering an enemy out of a mid-swing COMMIT in a four-body group and could not.

punish_read.trigger_player_states declares HEAL, ITEM and LONG_RECOVERY; the piece's M9 drives only the heal. Applying M9's own bar (>= 80% of trials) to a whiffed heavy over twelve settle offsets: HEAL 12/12 for every statblock, LONG_RECOVERY 7/12 for the four INFANTRY (below the bar), 10/12 champion, 11/12 beast, 12/12 caster. The cause is measured rather than guessed: the enemy was already committed at trial start in 7 of the 12 misses. Defensible Souls behaviour, but it means M9's 2/2 is a property of the heal fixture and the most common punishable moment in the game gets a coin flip from the enemy the player meets most often.

ai.json ships 13 frame-valued leaves and declares NO document-level `unit` field, while every statblock beside it does (inf_trash.json: "unit": "f@60"). Eight carry no machine-readable unit; five have neither a unit nor a seconds anchor in the source item. That matters because RI-AI01 was NOT in the wave-0 S22 rebase — REBASE-S22-REPORT.md §Job 1 names RI-CMB01/02/05/08, RI-AI02, RI-AI03, RI-WPN01-06 and RI-CAM04, fourteen items, and the item this piece is built against is not one of them. Where RI-AI01 gave SECONDS the builder converted at 60 Hz and every conversion checks out (token_hold_cap_f 180 <- 3.0 s; token_cooldown_f [54,90] <- 1.2 +/- 0.3 s; search_to_leash_frames 720 <- 12.0 s; feint_release_cooldown_f 36 <- +0.6 s). NO doubled or halved window was found and no 30-tick figure is compared to a 60 Hz one anywhere — the piece makes no comparison to Souls reference data at all. The one bare-f copy with a consequence is perception.aggro_entry_frames [20,30] from T05's mandatory aggro roar: 0.33-0.50 s at 60 Hz, 0.67-1.00 s if T05's f is a tick. The project's own reactability floor is t_react >= 19 f@60 = 317 ms (RI-CMB12 §A), so the shipped roar's lower bound clears the floor by 16 ms. Nobody can tell which reading is right because nobody wrote the unit down. Separately: I measured the one place §F could be being disobeyed and it is not — enemy.js:259 hard-codes a 180 deg/s windup steer against ai.json's declared 120, but the observed windup yaw rate is 36.5-57.9 deg/s with budgets 17.9-30.4 deg, inside RI-AI02 §C's trash row of 90 deg/s and 60 deg. Dead parameter, legal behaviour.

Arm A, delete the behaviour (ai.json enabled:false): every statblock collapses to a single state (REPOSITION or IDLE), 0 commits, 0 feints, entropy 0 — the AI is doing the work, not correlating with it. Arm B, delete the fix (the REPOSITION sprint back-off, ai.js:263-282): on the BUILDER'S fixture min_dist_dwell 0.041 -> 0.107 and M3 drops 2/2 -> 1/2, so the block is load-bearing and is what carries M3 over its line; on MY fixture the same block is worth 0.0035 -> 0.0049. Both arms differ from their control so neither is inert, but a block worth 0.066 on one fixture and 0.0014 on another says the headline is fixture-dominated, and the shipped margin (0.041 against a 0.10 pass) is 2.4x. Arm C, try to break the token by staggering an enemy out of a mid-swing COMMIT: no leak. All three ran on `cp -r game tools` into the scratchpad; game/src/combat/ and game/data/combat/ were clean and unstaged before and after (RULES 17).

tools/harness/ai-probe.mjs moves the player on p.pos[0] = 2.6*sin(i/140), p.pos[2] = 1.9*sin(i/97+1.1). Peak speed is 2.6/140*60 = 1.11 m/s in x and 1.9/97*60 = 1.18 m/s in z, about 1.6 m/s combined — BELOW this game's own 2.0 m/s walk (game/src/sim/state.js PLAYER_CONST). RULES 8 is satisfied in form (the target moves) and the survey demonstrates the still-fixture's bias honestly, but the entire speed range the piece's central question turns on — walk 2.0, jog 3.2, sprint 5.0 — sits outside the fixture that produced every headline number. It is also a teleporting player rather than one driven through the player controller.

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 is absent from the wave-0 S22 rebase and its §D table carries about twenty bare `f` figures whose unit has never been stated.
corpus_extended.why: S22 says in terms that a bare frame count is a defect and that ours must be written f@60 and a Souls tick t@30. The rebase moved fourteen items and this was not one of them, so a builder reading T05's '20-30 f' cannot tell whether the shipped aggro roar should be 0.33-0.50 s or 0.67-1.00 s — and neither can a critic. Filed as a corpus edge rather than charged to the piece, because the piece copied the item faithfully.
corpus_extended.proposed: Rebase and label RI-AI01, RI-AI04, RI-AI05, RI-AI06 and RI-AI07 the way Job 1 labelled RI-AI02 and RI-AI03, and add the `f@60` suffix to every frame column in RI-AI01 §D and §F.

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 M4's coefficient-of-variation hard fail does not detect the most timer-driven enemy in this project.
corpus_extended.why: Reported rather than exploited, and the builder found it first (reports/w1-12/survey.md §5e) — I confirm it independently. M4 hard-fails a build whose inter-COMMIT CoV is < 0.12, on the reasoning that a near-constant interval means a timer. character/encounter.js::engageMember is a pure timer (attack_cadence_f 78) and scores CoV ~0.3, because 78 f@60 is shorter than three of the four rotated attacks (154/122/72/102 f@60), so the interval is set by whichever animation is playing and a fixed rotation of unequal-length clips manufactures variance out of no decision at all.
corpus_extended.proposed: M4's CoV should be computed over the interval from the END of one COMMIT to the START of the next — the enemy's own decision gap — not from start to start, which is dominated by clip length.

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 §D declares RECOVER and STAGGER as behaviour-tree leaves but M3's denominator clause names only COMMIT, so a build that folds RECOVER into COMMIT passes a check the item intends it to fail.
corpus_extended.why: Measured: folding RECOVER into COMMIT moves min_dist_dwell from 0.0414 to 0.2521 on one enemy and flips M3 from 2/2 to 1/2 on all seven fighting statblocks. The item cannot currently tell a build that implements T15 from one that skips it.
corpus_extended.proposed: M3 should say 'while the enemy is in startup or active frames of an attack' rather than 'while state != COMMIT', so the check is a property of the fight and not of the build's state naming.

method_deviations.what: Wrote my own instrument rather than re-running the builder's.
method_deviations.why: RULES 22/23 and CRITIC-DOCTRINE: a probe that calls a function measures the function. tools/combat/critic-w1-12-census.mjs, -s22.mjs and -chart.mjs are mine, written with fresh context, and both census controls (a leaf that MUST move the trace and one that MUST NOT) make the tool exit non-zero if it goes blind or fires spuriously.
method_deviations.impact: None adverse. Where my numbers and the builder's differ (min_dist_dwell 0.0035 vs 0.041) the difference is the fixture, and I re-ran the decisive ablation on the BUILDER'S fixture and seed so the delete-the-fix comparison is apples to apples.

method_deviations.what: RI-AI01 M1 and M2 were not independently re-measured.
method_deviations.why: Both are entirely about how the perception meter FILLS, which the bare-Node arena does not run, and node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned exit 3 on every poll after the first (4 browser instances, load 21.55 over 4 cores). RULES 21: do the work that needs no browser.
method_deviations.impact: M1=1 and M2=2 are taken from the builder's own browser leg. If either is wrong my RI-AI01 total of 14/18 moves by up to 3. The three checks I moved (M3, M6, M9) are all measured by me in bare Node and are unaffected.

method_deviations.what: No blind pair, which RI-AI01 specifies (two anonymised 60 s dist_m + state series, ours against a reference generated from §C/§D).
method_deviations.why: Not built and not judged, so RULES 25 is not breached — but the blind evidence is simply absent rather than negative.
method_deviations.impact: RI-AI01's blind protocol contributes nothing to the 14/18. A round-2 critic should build the pack.

method_deviations.what: The census perturbation is x2 only, not two-sided.
method_deviations.why: One direction keeps the sweep to 104 leaves x 8 statblocks x 1,800 frames within budget on a box at load 26.
method_deviations.impact: A x2 on a threshold that is already satisfied is a no-op, so punish_read.band_multiple is reported as inert WITH that caveat rather than as dead. Six of the 29 no-consumer leaves carry an instrument caveat and are discounted in the verdict's headline of 23.

method_deviations.what: The B4 sight-cone ablation was read, not driven.
method_deviations.why: It needs the browser (stepEncounters wants sim.entities, a character and the world's encounter data).
method_deviations.impact: I confirmed by source read that encounter.js:214's `perceives` gate exists and reads real geometry (the statblock's own sight_cone_deg and e.percept_los), but I did not drive a sentry from three bearings myself. The builder's B4 result stands unchallenged rather than confirmed.

arbitration_questions.question: Does a derived Morrowind disposition deciding WHETHER an encounter is hostile — and therefore whether the Souls state machine ever enters its AGGRO branch — fall inside AR-1?
arbitration_questions.my_reading: No, and §7 of the .md sets out four reasons with the full call path. The disposition term is binary and never modulates a Souls quantity; ARBITRATION §1 puts the start of the fight at the aggro frame; AR-3 names exactly this shape as the crossing it wants; and S26 warns that a check firing on everything distinguishes nothing. Filed rather than invented because the boundary is one line wide — `aggro_at_m: 18 - disposition/5` would cross it — and a future critic should argue with this paragraph rather than re-derive it.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-AI01 was excluded from the wave-0 S22 rebase. Should it be rebased, and if so is T05's '20-30 f' aggro roar 20-30 t@30 (i.e. 40-60 f@60) or already f@60?
arbitration_questions.my_reading: The item must be rebased and labelled — S22 says a bare frame count is a defect and RI-AI01 carries about twenty of them, with ai.json copying several across verbatim. I cannot answer the T05 question from inside the corpus, which is the point: the roar as shipped is 0.33-0.50 s, 16 ms above this project's own reactability floor at its lower bound, and doubles to 0.67-1.00 s under the other reading. That is not a rounding difference on the one parameter that governs the moment the player is told a fight has begun.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE: RI-AI01 M1 and M2 were not independently re-measured because they need the perception model the bare-Node arena does not run and the contention gate refused a browser on every poll after the first; they are taken from the builder's browser leg and named in method_deviations with their impact. The B4 sight-cone ablation was read rather than driven, for the same reason. blind_done_where_required is FALSE: RI-AI01 specifies a blind pair and I neither built nor judged one — absent evidence, not negative evidence, and RULES 25 is not breached because I built no pack. Neither absence is load-bearing for the FAIL, which rests on three measurements I took myself in bare Node over the shipping modules: the flee sweep (§2), the RECOVER recomputation of M3 on the builder's own fixture and seed (§1), and the 104-leaf consumption census with two working controls (§3).
